message.reasoning_content:
The kernel: computes sigmoid via exp(-|x|) trick, div_rn, then cvt.rn.f16.f32 rounding. Potential issues: intermediate exp in fp32 introduces rounding errors, so final FP16 might not be exactly the correctly-rounded FP64 sigmoid. Test all finite FP16 values exhaustively (65536 minus NaN/Inf) against FP64 reference rounded to FP16.

Also note the -0.0 input: x<0? -0.0 < 0.0 is false in IEEE, so numerator=1, exp=1, result 0.5. Good.

Let me record a claim and run exhaustive probe.

Concern: reference() uses struct.pack('<e') — that's half precision? '<e' is binary16 in struct — yes. But rounding of FP64→binary16 in struct: round-to-nearest-even. Good.

Probe: iterate over all 65536 fp16 bit patterns, run kernel.run, compare to reference. N=131072 max, so split into chunks. Use bits > bits conversion on GPU.
